topic: Understanding Distribution Channels – Concept & Progress
t: Which of the following is NOT one of the classical functions performed by channel intermediaries?
o: Manufacturing the core product
Negotiating price and terms with buyers
Financing inventory and assuming risk
Gathering and sharing market information
e: Intermediaries perform information, promotion, contact, matching, negotiation, physical distribution, financing and risk-taking functions. Manufacturing the core product remains with the producer.

topic: Understanding Distribution Channels – Concept & Progress
t: Before the opening of the Indian insurance sector in 2000, life insurance distribution in India was dominated by:
o: The individual tied agency force of LIC
Bank branches acting as corporate agents
Composite insurance brokers
Online web aggregators
e: Until liberalisation, LIC's large individual agency force was effectively the only life distribution channel. Corporate agents, brokers and aggregators were introduced by IRDAI regulations after 2000.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: 'Intensive distribution' is a strategy in which the producer:
o: Sells only through its own retail stores
Uses only a small number of carefully selected outlets
Places the product in as many outlets as possible
Restricts sales to one dealer per territory
e: Intensive distribution maximises availability through many outlets (typical for convenience goods). Exclusive distribution uses one dealer per territory and selective distribution uses a limited set of outlets.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: A life insurer decides to sell through its own agents, several banks, two brokers and its website simultaneously. This approach is called:
o: Vertical integration
Exclusive distribution
Channel captaincy
Multi-channel distribution
e: Using several channel types to reach customers is multi-channel (or hybrid) distribution. It widens reach but raises the possibility of channel conflict and higher coordination cost.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: Which of the following is the FIRST step in designing a distribution channel?
o: Analysing the customer's service output needs
Setting channel member incentives
Selecting and training channel members
Evaluating the economic cost of each alternative
e: Channel design starts with understanding what service outputs customers want (lot size, waiting time, convenience, variety, service backup); objectives, alternatives and evaluation follow.

topic: Channel Mix Decisions and Distribution Strategy
t: A general insurer finds that its agency channel brings in motor business at an acquisition cost of 18% of premium, while its direct website brings it at 6%. The insurer should most appropriately:
o: Raise agency commission to match the website cost
Compare the channels on persistency, claims quality, volume and customer segment before changing the mix
Ignore the data because channel cost is irrelevant to strategy
Close the agency channel immediately because it costs more
e: Channel mix decisions weigh cost against reach, volume, business quality and customer preference. Acquisition cost alone does not justify eliminating a channel that may serve segments the website cannot.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Under the Insurance Act, 1938 as amended in 2015, an individual insurance agent is:
o: Appointed by the insurer, who is responsible for the agent's conduct
Licensed by IRDAI after a central examination
Registered with the Insurance Ombudsman
Licensed by the state government
e: The 2015 amendment to Section 42 shifted agents from IRDAI licensing to appointment by insurers under the IRDAI (Appointment of Insurance Agents) Regulations, 2016, with insurers accountable for their agents.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: An insurer's data shows that 20% of its agents bring in 80% of its premium. This observation is an application of:
o: The gaps model
The Pareto principle
SERVQUAL
Net Promoter Score
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 80/20 (Pareto) rule suggests concentrating management attention and support on the vital few high-performing agents and the most valuable customers.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A 'composite' individual insurance agent in India may hold agency of:
o: Only one insurer in total
Up to three insurers in each category
Any number of life insurers but only one general insurer
One life insurer, one general insurer, one health insurer and one of each mono-line insurer
e: An individual may be agent of one life, one general, one health insurer and one each of the mono-line insurers (e.g. Agriculture Insurance Company, ECGC). Holding multiple agencies in the same category is prohibited.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: After the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents Regulations, a corporate agent may have arrangements with a maximum of:
o: Three insurers in each of the life, general and health categories
Six insurers in total across all categories
One insurer in each category
Nine insurers in each of the life, general and health categories
e: The limit was raised from three to nine insurers per category (life, general, health) in 2022 to widen open architecture and customer choice at bank and other corporate-agent counters.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Brokers) Regulations, 2018, the minimum paid-up capital for a direct insurance broker is:
o: ₹25 lakh
₹50 lakh
₹75 lakh
₹4 crore
e: Direct brokers need ₹75 lakh capital; reinsurance brokers ₹4 crore and composite brokers ₹5 crore. ₹25 lakh is the web-aggregator capital and ₹50 lakh is the direct broker's minimum net worth.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The fundamental difference between an insurance agent and an insurance broker is that:
o: An agent represents the insurer while a broker represents the customer and can deal with multiple insurers
Only agents are regulated by IRDAI
Brokers can sell only general insurance
A broker represents the insurer while an agent represents the customer
e: An agent is the insurer's representative appointed to solicit business; a broker is an independent professional acting on behalf of the client and may place business with any insurer.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Which of the following is a key MERIT of the bancassurance channel?
o: Bancassurance eliminates mis-selling completely
Banks are exempt from IRDAI code of conduct
Bank staff are necessarily better trained in insurance than agents
Banks already have an existing customer base, trust and transaction data enabling low-cost reach
e: Bancassurance leverages the bank's customer base, branch network and data for low-cost cross-selling. Mis-selling and limited product knowledge are, in fact, recognised demerits of the channel.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: An insurance web aggregator is permitted to:
o: Settle claims directly
Collect premium in its own bank account for retention
Display and compare products of different insurers and pass leads to them
Underwrite policies on behalf of insurers
e: Web aggregators maintain a website that displays and compares product information of insurers and transmits leads; they do not underwrite, hold premium or settle claims.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The Point of Sales Person (POSP) channel was created by IRDAI mainly to:
o: Sell complex unit-linked plans to high-net-worth customers
Replace the broker channel
Handle reinsurance placements
Distribute simple, pre-underwritten products through a person with minimal training
e: POSPs (min. age 18, 10th pass, 15 hours training with examination by the insurer or intermediary) sell simple, standardised products where underwriting is largely automatic at the point of sale.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: Under the 2022 amendment, an Insurance Marketing Firm (IMF) may solicit business for up to:
o: Six insurers in each of the life, general and health categories
Unlimited insurers in each category
Nine insurers in each category
Two insurers in each category
e: IMF tie-up limits were raised from two to six insurers in each of life, general and health. Nine is the corporate-agent limit; brokers have no tie-up restriction.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A reinsurance broker's main role is to:
o: Aggregate online leads
Sell retail motor policies to individuals
Act as a corporate agent of a bank
Arrange reinsurance placements for insurers (cedants) with reinsurers
e: A reinsurance broker intermediates between insurers seeking reinsurance and reinsurers. A composite broker does both direct and reinsurance broking.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: The foreign direct investment limit in Indian insurance companies was raised to 74% by the Insurance (Amendment) Act of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). FDI was 26% from 2000, raised to 49% in 2015 and to 74% in 2021, to bring more capital for growth and distribution expansion.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: A major DEMERIT of the individual agency channel in life insurance is:
o: Agents cannot be appointed by private insurers
It cannot offer personalised advice
High attrition of agents and consequent orphan policies and poor persistency
It is illegal for agents to collect premium
e: Agency gives face-to-face advice but suffers from high agent turnover, which leaves policies without servicing agents and hurts persistency; recruitment and training costs are also high.

topic: Distribution Channels in Insurance – Merits and Demerits
t: The direct (online) channel of an insurer is most suitable for:
o: Group gratuity schemes
Large commercial property risks
Complex, high-value participating policies requiring extensive advice
Simple, standardised products such as term life, motor and travel insurance
e: Online direct sales work for products that customers can understand and buy without advice. Complex or large commercial risks still require intermediaries' advice and negotiation.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: 'Customer perceived value' is defined as:
o: The commission paid to the distributor
The difference between the total benefits the customer receives and the total costs the customer incurs
The sum assured under the policy
The price paid for the product
e: Perceived value is total customer benefit (product, service, personnel, image) minus total customer cost (monetary, time, energy, psychic). Distribution adds value by raising benefits or reducing costs.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: Which of the following is NOT one of the five SERVQUAL dimensions of service quality?
o: Responsiveness
Empathy
Reliability
Profitability
e: SERVQUAL (Parasuraman, Zeithaml and Berry) measures reliability, assurance, tangibles, empathy and responsiveness (RATER). Profitability is a firm outcome, not a service-quality dimension.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: A 'moment of truth' in service marketing refers to:
o: The date of claim settlement only
Any interaction in which the customer forms an impression of the organisation's service quality
The signing of the proposal form
The underwriting decision
e: Coined by Jan Carlzon, a moment of truth is every customer contact point that shapes perception. For insurance, agent visits, premium reminders and claim handling are all such moments.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: A distributor who reduces the customer's time and effort by completing the proposal digitally and explaining the product in simple language is primarily adding value by:
o: Reducing the customer's non-monetary costs
Lowering the insurer's solvency margin
Increasing the policy term
Raising the sum assured
e: Customer cost includes time, energy and psychic cost. Making purchase convenient and understandable reduces these non-monetary costs and therefore increases perceived value.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: In the 'service-profit chain', employee satisfaction is linked to profit through:
o: Higher commission rates
Service value leading to customer satisfaction and loyalty, which drives revenue growth and profit
Reduction in claims
Lower reinsurance costs
e: The service-profit chain argues that satisfied, productive employees deliver better service value, creating satisfied and loyal customers, which in turn drives growth and profitability.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Life insurance is often said to be 'sold, not bought'. This implies that:
o: Distribution must create need-awareness and persuade, because customers rarely initiate purchase
Insurers do not need distribution channels
Customers actively seek out insurance without persuasion
Insurance cannot be sold online
e: Because the benefit is intangible and deferred, customers seldom come forward on their own; hence the central role of a persuasive, advice-driven distribution force in life insurance.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Information asymmetry' in insurance distribution refers to the situation where:
o: One party (customer or insurer) has more relevant information than the other, creating risks such as adverse selection and mis-selling
Policy documents are in different languages
Agents are paid different commission rates
The insurer always knows more than the customer
e: The proposer knows more about his own risk (adverse selection), while the insurer and distributor know more about the product (potential mis-selling). Distribution must bridge both gaps through disclosure and advice.

topic: Creating Customer Value through Distribution
t: An agent explains the claims process clearly, hands over the policy personally within a week and calls after 30 days to check understanding. In SERVQUAL terms, these actions mainly strengthen:
o: Tangibles only
Reliability, responsiveness and empathy
Profitability
Solvency
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Timely delivery (reliability), prompt attention (responsiveness) and caring follow-up (empathy) raise perceived service quality and therefore customer value.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Which of the following is a characteristic of insurance that makes its distribution more challenging than that of physical goods?
o: It is tangible and can be inspected before purchase
It is a promise whose benefit is uncertain and may be realised far in the future
It has no regulatory oversight
It requires no documentation
e: Insurance is an intangible promise of future performance; the customer cannot test it before purchase and may never experience the benefit, which places a heavy burden on the channel to build trust.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: Insurance penetration is measured as:
o: Premium as a percentage of GDP
Claims paid as a percentage of premium
Per-capita premium in US dollars
Number of policies per 1,000 population
e: Penetration is total premium divided by GDP. Insurance density is per-capita premium (premium divided by population). India's low penetration is the key distribution opportunity.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: A life insurer's 13th-month persistency ratio of 72% (by number of policies) means that:
o: The insurer's expense ratio is 72%
28% of agents left within 13 months
72% of claims were settled within 13 months
72% of the policies sold a year earlier were still in force after the first renewal premium fell due
e: Persistency measures retention of policies at a specified duration. Low 13th-month persistency indicates mis-selling or poor need analysis at the point of sale.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: IRDAI's rural and social sector obligations affect distribution strategy because they:
o: Require insurers to write a minimum share of business in rural areas and among social-sector lives, pushing them to build low-cost rural channels
Apply only to LIC
Prohibit insurers from selling in urban areas
Fix commission at 5% for all rural policies
e: The obligations require every insurer to achieve prescribed rural and social-sector targets, which drives the use of micro-insurance agents, CSCs, IMFs and Bima Vahaks.

topic: Unique Aspects of Insurance Distribution: Opportunities and Challenges
t: 'Adverse selection' is the tendency of:
o: Customers to buy only the cheapest plan
Persons with higher-than-average risk to seek insurance more actively than low-risk persons
Insurers to reject all proposals
Agents to sell only to friends and relatives
e: Adverse selection results from information asymmetry: high-risk individuals are more inclined to buy cover. Underwriting and well-trained distributors mitigate it.

topic: Policyholder protection
t: The IRDAI portal through which a policyholder can escalate an unresolved grievance against an insurer is:
o: Bima Sugam
Bima Bharosa
Bima Vahak
Bima Vistaar
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bima Bharosa (formerly IGMS) is the grievance portal; Bima Sugam is the marketplace, Bima Vahak the women-led distribution channel and Bima Vistaar the combined rural product.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) is:
o: The sum assured on the customer's largest policy
The commission earned on the first policy
The present value of the net profit expected from a customer over the entire relationship
The number of years the customer has held a policy
e: CLV estimates the total discounted contribution from a customer across all purchases, renewals and referrals, and is used to decide how much to invest in acquiring and retaining each customer.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: 'Operational CRM' refers to:
o: Sharing information with channel partners
Regulatory reporting
Statistical analysis of customer data to find patterns
Automation of customer-facing processes such as sales, marketing and service
e: CRM is commonly classified as operational (front-office automation), analytical (data mining and segmentation) and collaborative (sharing across partners and channels).

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: It is generally stated that acquiring a new customer costs about five times as much as retaining an existing one. For an insurer, this most directly justifies investment in:
o: Lower sum assured
Higher first-year commission
Renewal servicing, cross-selling and persistency management
More television advertising
e: Because retention is far cheaper than acquisition, CRM focuses the channel on servicing existing policyholders, improving persistency and cross-selling to them.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: Net Promoter Score (NPS) is calculated as:
o: Average of all scores on a 10-point scale
Number of complaints per 1,000 policies
Percentage of Promoters (score 9–10) minus percentage of Detractors (score 0–6)
Promoters plus Passives minus Detractors
e: NPS asks how likely the customer is to recommend the firm; Promoters score 9–10, Passives 7–8, Detractors 0–6. NPS = %Promoters − %Detractors.

topic: Customer Relationship Management through Distribution
t: An agent who sells a health policy to an existing term-life customer is engaged in:
o: Up-selling
Cross-selling
Rebating
Twisting
e: Cross-selling offers a different product category to an existing customer; up-selling moves the customer to a higher-value version of the same product. Rebating and twisting are prohibited practices.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: 'Need-based selling' in insurance means:
o: Recommending products after assessing the customer's financial goals, existing cover and capacity to pay
Selling the plan with the highest commission
Selling only products the agent personally holds
Meeting the agent's monthly target by any means
e: Need-based selling starts with a fact-find and needs analysis, so that the recommended product is suitable; this reduces mis-selling and improves persistency.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: The purpose of a pre-issuance verification call (PIVC) by a life insurer is to:
o: Train the agent
Confirm that the customer understands the product features, premium and term before the policy is issued
Collect the renewal premium
Reduce the free-look period
e: PIVC is a mis-selling control: the insurer independently confirms the customer's understanding of key features, premium paying term and benefits before issuing the policy.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024, the free-look period for a policy is:
o: 15 days for all policies
30 days for all policies irrespective of mode of sale
15 days for physical sale and 30 days for electronic sale
45 days for life and 15 days for general
e: From 2024 the free-look period was made a uniform 30 days from receipt of the policy document for all policies, replacing the earlier 15/30-day distinction by sales mode.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: Which practice by an agent is prohibited under the agents' code of conduct?
o: Informing the insurer of material facts about the proposer
Offering the customer a share of commission as inducement to buy
Disclosing the commission to the customer on request
Explaining the nature of exclusions
e: Sharing commission with the customer is rebating, prohibited under Section 41 of the Insurance Act, 1938 (penalty up to ₹10 lakh). The other acts are required conduct.

topic: Best Practices in Distribution Management in Insurance
t: A life insurer links a portion of the agent's reward to 13th-month and 25th-month persistency. This best practice aims to:
o: Reduce the agent's income
Increase first-year commission
Align the agent's incentives with selling suitable policies that stay in force
Comply with the Insurance Ombudsman Rules
e: Persistency-linked compensation discourages churning and mis-selling by rewarding agents for business that continues, aligning distributor and insurer interests.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: IRDAI's stated vision 'Insurance for All' targets the year:
e: IRDAI aims for every citizen to have appropriate life, health and property cover and every enterprise to have suitable insurance by 2047, the centenary of India's independence.

topic: Policyholder protection
t: An insurer must resolve a policyholder's grievance within how many days of receipt?
o: 7 days
14 days
30 days
45 days
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 14 days under the 2024 regulations; thereafter the policyholder may approach Bima Bharosa or the Ombudsman.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: 'Bima Sugam' is:
o: A composite product bundling life, health and property cover
A women-centric field distribution force
A digital insurance marketplace for buying, selling, servicing and claims across insurers
A grievance redressal portal
e: Bima Sugam is the electronic marketplace set up under IRDAI's 2024 regulations. Bima Vahak is the women-centric field force and Bima Vistaar is the composite product; the grievance portal is Bima Bharosa.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: Under the 2022 reforms, private equity funds were permitted to:
o: Invest directly in insurance companies without routing through a Special Purpose Vehicle
Act as insurance brokers
Underwrite reinsurance
Appoint insurance agents
e: IRDAI simplified capital raising by allowing PE funds to invest directly in insurers, removing the earlier requirement of an SPV structure.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: The IRDAI Regulatory Sandbox is intended to:
o: Fix the commission payable to agents
Test innovative products, processes and distribution ideas in a controlled environment with relaxed regulations for a limited period
Replace the Insurance Act, 1938
Register new insurance brokers
e: The sandbox allows insurers and intermediaries to pilot innovations such as usage-based, blockchain-enabled or cyber covers under IRDAI supervision before full regulatory roll-out.

topic: IRDAI Initiatives towards Expansion of Insurance Business
t: A general insurer has gross written premium of ₹2,000 crore in a financial year. Under the IRDAI Expenses of Management regulations, its overall expenses of management (including commission) are normally capped at:
e: General insurers are allowed EoM up to 30% of gross written premium in India; standalone health insurers get 35%. 30% of ₹2,000 crore = ₹600 crore.
